explanation: Dysplasia = disorganized, reversible. Anaplasia = loss of differentiation, irreversible, hallmark of malignancy.

subject: Pathology
question: Which of the following statements best describes dysplasia in pathology?

options.A: An irreversible change where one mature cell type is replaced by another mature cell type.
options.B: A reversible decrease in the size and number of cells in an organ or tissue.
options.C: A disordered, non-neoplastic proliferation of cells characterized by loss of uniform structure and cellular atypia.
options.D: The complete failure of an organ to develop due to the absence of primordium.

explanation: Dysplasia refers to a loss of architectural organization and cellular uniformity (pleomorphism, hyperchromatic nuclei) that is considered a pre-malignant change but has not yet invaded the basement membrane (i.e., it is non-neoplastic).
